- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near-zero — model fails to capture downward pressure or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 2–4 days; adjust for delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.
- After sharp upward spikes in sentiment, model often overcorrects and forecasts a peak too early — reduce forecast peak by 10–15% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecasts with 3-day moving average or apply sentiment-weighted dampening.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently overpredicts late-period prices (last 7–10 days) — apply downward correction of 3–8% for final 10 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
